title: Methotrexate: head and neck cancer
context_label: Recurrent or advanced head and neck cancer
indication_text: Recurrent, advanced or metastatic head and neck squamous cell cancer in people with comorbidities or unsuitable for combination chemotherapy.
purpose: This treatment aims to slow cancer growth and help control symptoms. Your team explains the expected benefit, uncertainty and alternatives for your situation.
cycle_display: IV on Days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days
schedule_label: IV on Days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days
schedule_summary: Methotrexate 40 mg/m² by intravenous bolus on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. There is no scheduled Day-22 dose. The clinician may increase to 50 mg/m² only if there has been no mucositis.
administration_text: Methotrexate is given into a vein by the treatment team. This is an intermittent intravenous cancer regimen, not a daily tablet schedule. Check the written appointment calendar before each visit. Never take extra methotrexate yourself.

agents.name: Methotrexate
agents.explanation: Methotrexate interferes with folate-dependent reactions that cells need to make DNA. This can slow cancer-cell division, while also affecting blood-cell production and the lining of the mouth and bowel.
agents.watch: Tell the pharmacist about all painkillers, antibiotics, supplements and other medicines because interactions can increase methotrexate toxicity. Report new cough or breathlessness, mouth ulcers, unusual bleeding, jaundice, reduced urine or severe rash promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, infection, bruising and bleeding
Kidney or liver injury; accumulation with impaired kidney clearance
Rare lung inflammation and severe skin reactions
Fertility effects and risks in pregnancy or breastfeeding

anatomy: Balance activity and rest. Sudden confusion, seizure, severe headache or a change in vision needs urgent help.
Report ulcers, pain, dry mouth, difficulty swallowing or weight loss early. Ask for oral care, dietetic and swallowing support.
Fever, shivering, sudden illness, unusual bruising or bleeding needs urgent oncology advice.
New cough or breathlessness needs prompt review; serious causes include infection or lung injury.
Use prescribed support. Report persistent diarrhoea or vomiting, inability to drink, blood or severe abdominal pain.
Report reduced urine, swelling or poor fluid intake; keep blood and urine tests.
Report painful palms or soles, rash or blistering early. Severe spreading rash or mouth/eye involvement needs urgent review.
Discuss fertility preservation, contraception, pregnancy and breastfeeding before starting.

support.text: Follow the unit’s mouth-care plan. Report pain, poor intake or weight loss early; ask for dietetic support. Pace activity, rest and work around symptoms.

evidence.title: What the evidence can tell you
evidence.intro: Research supports a treatment discussion; it cannot predict one person’s outcome.
evidence.population: Recurrent, advanced or metastatic head and neck squamous cell cancer in people with comorbidities or unsuitable for combination chemotherapy.
evidence.comparison: Limited evidence for this specific regimen and setting
evidence.interpretation: The source cites methotrexate experience in recurrent head and neck cancer. Evidence must be interpreted for this exact 40 mg/m² intravenous Days 1, 8 and 15 schedule. Results from other weekly doses or combinations should not be presented as established benefit for this regimen.
limitations: Small studies and mixed tumour groups limit certainty.
Other doses or combinations cannot be assumed equivalent.

consent_support: Discuss treatment aim, expected benefit and uncertainty, alternatives and the option of declining; each medicine’s risks, potentially lasting effects, required tests, urgent symptoms, fertility, contraception, pregnancy, breastfeeding and the individual support plan. Report new cough or breathlessness, mouth ulcers, unusual bleeding, jaundice, reduced urine or severe rash promptly.
